title: Region atlas
description: A per-game map partition: the real game's tile map divided into procgen regions, with boundary/teleporter exits, per-region sub-region subgraphs, locations, and the vanilla layout (CC/docs/plans/region-atlas-plan.md, Phase 1). One authored document per game, stored beside the game's wrapper, edited by the region-marking tool, and compiled into three projections (vanilla rules.json / sphere-sorter input / play-time payload). This schema is DOCUMENTATION: the cross-reference rules it cannot express (content-hash identity, sub-region referential integrity + reachability, edge-exit geometry, vanilla_layout endpoint resolution, Rule Builder tree shape) are enforced authoritatively by frontend/modules/procgenPipeline/regionAtlasValidator.js.

atlas_id.description: Stamped content-hash id; ends with '-<content_hash>'. Downstream pipeline steps key on it, so an edited document must be restamped (that restamp is what invalidates them).

game.description: The game this atlas maps (e.g. 'seedling'). Engine-binding mechanics for the game live in its wrapper config (flashPanel games/<id>.json), NOT here — the atlas holds map semantics only.

content_hash.description: FNV-1a over the canonical (sorted-key) document minus provenance and atlas_id; atlas_id must end with '-<content_hash>'. Restamp with scripts/procgen/region-atlas-validate.mjs --restamp after a hand edit.

tile_space.description: The coordinate system every tile/bounds value in this document is expressed in. Tile coordinates are absolute in the game's own map space; y grows DOWNWARD (so side 'N' is the minimum-y row).

tile_size.description: Pixels per tile in the source map.

map_source.description: Where the tile map came from, e.g. 'runtime-extract'. The atlas never embeds the tile grid — it references it (plan decision 7).

map_document.description: Filename of the map-source document these coordinates live in, resolved relative to the atlas file (e.g. 'seedling-map.json'). Required once any region carries map_ref.

vanilla_layout.description: The original game's own wiring. Map truth, and the input the vanilla-rules.json projection needs (plan decision 4).

start_sub_region.description: Required when the start region has a subgraph (otherwise the projection cannot tell which sub-region Menu connects to); forbidden when it does not.

connections.description: Undirected pairings of exits. Each endpoint is [region_id, exit_id] and may appear in at most one connection. Edge/edge pairs are normally opposite sides (N↔S, E↔W); teleporter endpoints need not be grid neighbours.

rule.description: An ordinary Rule Builder rule tree, exactly as the pipeline emits into rules.json — e.g. {"rule": "Has", "args": {"item_name": "Progressive Swim"}} or {"rule": "And", "children": [...]}. See frontend/schema/rules.schema.json $defs/ruleBuilderRule. The validator checks the tree's SHAPE only; rule names may be game-specific helpers.

args.description: Object for named args, array for positional args.

region_id.description: Unique within the atlas. Must NOT contain '__': the AP projection names a sub-region '<region_id>__<sub_region>' (see apRegionName in the validator), so the separator has to stay unambiguous.

bounds.description: The region's tile rectangle in absolute tile space. Every exit tile and location tile must lie inside it.

map_ref.description: Which coordinate space this region's bounds and tiles live in: the id of a level in tile_space.map_document. A game whose map is ONE space (RWK) omits it; a game built of many per-level spaces (Seedling: 116 levels, each with its own origin) names one per region. Geometry checks never cross regions, so this adds only the resolution check — and only when the map document is available to the validator.

exits.description: Boundary exits. An exit is a LOGICAL edge with a multi-tile span (exit_tiles) and a single arrival spawn point (entrance_tile).

subgraph.description: OPTIONAL. Present only when the region's interior has traversal obstacles (plan decision 1). When ABSENT the region is one implicit sub-region and every exit/location MUST omit `sub_region`; when PRESENT every exit/location MUST name one. A single-entry subgraph is redundant — omit the subgraph instead.

sub_regions.description: Local ids, unique within the region, no '__' (see region_id).

internal_exits.description: The traversal obstacles, as directed (or bidirectional) edges carrying the rule that crosses them. A one-way drop is bidirectional:false.

source.description: Who authored this row. ABSENT means 'manual' (every atlas written before the analyzer existed). Re-analysis replaces only its own rows; manual rows survive byte-exact.

name.description: AP location name; unique across the whole atlas.

sub_region.description: Required iff the region has a subgraph.

vanilla_item.description: What the original game puts here; the vanilla rules.json projection places it.

access_rule.description: OPTIONAL extra condition beyond reaching the sub-region (e.g. defeating a guard).

rules_source.description: Where this region's access rules came from. DERIVED from the subgraph's internal_exits[].source once any of them is 'analyzer': all-analyzer => 'analyzer', a mix => 'mixed'. A region with no analyzer rows is whatever the author says. Puzzle-gated games (Seedling) force hand-authored rows — that is expected, not a gap.

exit_id.description: Unique within its region; vanilla_layout references [region_id, exit_id].

kind.description: 'edge' = a straight boundary run whose direction gives the side label. Anything that does not fit a side (stairs, doors, warps) is a first-class 'teleporter' whose destination need not be a grid neighbour (plan decision 3).

side.description: Required for kind 'edge', forbidden for 'teleporter'. The exit_tiles must form a contiguous run along that side of `bounds` (N = minimum y).

exit_tiles.description: The tiles that trigger the transition. All inside `bounds`, no duplicates.

entrance_tile.description: Where the player spawns when ARRIVING through this exit. Must be one of exit_tiles — exits are logical edges, the entrance is a spawn point.

sub_region.description: Required iff the region has a subgraph.

access_rule.description: OPTIONAL intrinsic gate on the exit itself (a locked door). The sphere sorter reads these as the region's frontier rules.
